backward_compat_traps.rule: UFS 4.0 endpoints must negotiate the highest mutually supported HS-Gear during link startup; they begin in PWM/low gear.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A host that assumes HS-Gear 5 without negotiation, or that fails to fall back, will not link up with a lower-gear device.

backward_compat_traps.rule: UFSHCI 4.0 supports both the legacy single Transfer Request List (doorbell per task tag) and native MCQ; the model in use is configured by the host.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A driver that hard-codes the legacy doorbell model will not exploit MCQ parallelism, and a driver assuming MCQ on a controller that only advertises legacy mode will fail.

backward_compat_traps.rule: The RPMB 256-bit authentication key can be programmed exactly once and never read back.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Re-provisioning flows that attempt to reprogram the key will fail; the key must be escrowed at first provisioning.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Host Performance Booster is OPTIONAL (added UFS 3.1); not all devices implement it.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A host relying on HPB L2P caching must first verify device support via the Device Descriptor / flags before enabling fHpbEn.

key_changes.summary: Doubled per-lane rate to 11.6 Gbit/s (HS-Gear 4) via M-PHY 4.1 + UniPro 1.8.
Added WriteBooster turbo-write buffer + Host Performance Booster (optional L2P caching in host DRAM).
Doubled per-lane rate to 23.2 Gbit/s (HS-Gear 5) via M-PHY 5.0 + UniPro 2.0; added UFSHCI 4.0 native Multi-Circular Queue (MCQ) and File Based Optimization.

fields.version_naming_history_note: UFS is standardized by the JEDEC Solid State Technology Association as JESD220 (device) and JESD223 (UFSHCI host controller interface). The physical and transport layers are MIPI Alliance specifications (M-PHY and UniPro). The Universal Flash Storage Association (UFSA) was founded in 2010 to promote the standard. UFS is the JEDEC successor to eMMC; both share JEDEC stewardship, but UFS replaces eMMC's parallel half-duplex CMD/DAT bus with a full-duplex M-PHY/UniPro serial link and a SCSI/UPIU command model.

spec_lineage_emmc_predecessor.summary: Predecessor JEDEC mobile-storage family; parallel half-duplex CMD/DAT bus; HS400 strobe-based 200 MHz DDR.
Added Command Queueing (CQ) and Secure Removal; UFS is positioned as eMMC's successor with a full-duplex M-PHY/UniPro serial link and SCSI/UPIU model.
